summary: 从想象一个没有音乐、文学和绘画的世界出发，作者区分艺术能带来的益处与艺术存在的目的。艺术可以呈现美，也可以表达创作者对外界和内心经验的复杂反应，使他人获得新的感受。
logic: 从外部世界到内心体验

paragraphs.brief: 想象一下，在这样一个世界里，人们在办公室或工厂里工作了几个小时，然后在晚上回家吃晚饭，然后他们睡觉，直到起床工作的时候。
sentences: Imagine a world in which people spend hours working in offices or factories, and then go home in the evening to sit down to dinner, after which they sleep until it’s time to get up and work again.
想象一下，在这样一个世界里，人们在办公室或工厂里工作了几个小时，然后在晚上回家吃晚饭，然后他们睡觉，直到起床工作的时候。
In this world, people do not read or watch TV, listen to music, play computer games or have pictures to decorate their homes.
在这个世界上，人们不阅读或看电视，不听音乐，不玩电脑游戏，也不拍照来装饰他们的家。
In fact, there are no pictures in this world—not even advertisements are illustrated, but all are words, and very plain ones at that, with no playfulness left in them.
事实上，世界上没有图片，甚至连广告也没有，但都是文字，而且非常简单，没有留下任何乐趣。
The buildings are completely functional without a single decorative feature anywhere, and there is no music to dance to and enjoy.
这些建筑完全正常运转，任何地方都没有装饰功能，没有音乐可以跳舞和享受。
Such a world is a world without the arts in any form.
这样一个世界是一个没有任何形式的艺术的世界。

paragraphs.brief: 但同样，艺术家们可能只是做一件艺术作品因为他们觉得自己是迫不得已的
sentences: To ask what the arts are good for is not exactly the same as asking what their purpose is.
问艺术有什么用与问它们的目的并不完全相同

The arts do not have to have a purpose—they do not exist in order to teach, to make a moral point, to entertain, to distract, to amuse, to support a revolution, to disgust, to challenge, to stimulate or to cheer; they exist chiefly for their own sake.
艺术不必有目的——它们的存在不是为了教书、提出道德观点、娱乐、分散注意力、娱乐、支持革命、厌恶、挑战、激励或欢呼；它们的存在主要是为了其自身。
It is artists, not the arts as such, that may have an aim in mind, and their aim may be to do any of the things just listed.
艺术家，而不是艺术本身，可能有一个目标，他们的目标可能是做任何刚刚列出的事情。
But equally, artists may just make a work of art because they feel compelled to.
但同样，艺术家们可能只是做一件艺术作品因为他们觉得自己是迫不得已的
Because the work is its own justification, no aim or goal is necessarily required to explain or, still less, to justify its existence.
由于这项工作是其本身的理由，因此，不一定要求任何目的或目标来解释，更不必说，说明其存在的理由。

paragraphs.brief: 艺术的 " 优点 " 在于它们本身是目的，或者更准确地说，代表着许多对其本身来说有价值的不同事物，例如，创造美。
sentences: But to say that the arts do not have to serve an aim beyond themselves, even though they may sometimes do so, is not to say that they are good for nothing.
但是，说艺术不必服务于自己之外的目的，即使他们有时可能这样做，也不是说他们一无是处。
On the contrary, as such an important part of human experience, they are good for many things.
相反，作为人类经历的一个重要部分，它们对于许多事情都是好的。
The distinction here lies between things that are instrumental and things that are ends in themselves.
这里的区别在于那些工具和那些目的本身。
An instrument exists for something beyond itself—namely, for what it can be used to do.
一种工具存在于它本身之外，即它能够用来做什么。
We know that pictures are used as instruments in advertising, and the objective is always to persuade us to buy something.
我们知道图片是用来做广告的工具目的总是要说服我们买东西
Similarly, music can be written chiefly to accompany dancing, or as a soundtrack to a movie.
同样，音乐可以主要用来配合舞蹈，或者作为电影的音轨。
A play can be written to point out to the theatre audience a social injustice or other problems that should be dealt with.
剧本可以写给剧团观众指出社会不公或应该处理的其他问题。
But even though the arts can sometimes be instrumental, that fact is not essential to their nature.
但是，即使艺术有时可以起到作用，但这一事实对于其性质并不重要。

What the arts are ‘good for’ arises from their being an end in themselves, or more accurately, representing many different things that are valuable for their own sakes—such as, for instance, the creation of beauty.
艺术的 " 优点 " 在于它们本身是目的，或者更准确地说，代表着许多对其本身来说有价值的不同事物，例如，创造美。

paragraphs.brief: “艺术”一词包括绘画、雕塑、音乐、文学、舞蹈和戏剧表演等(引用美国著名艺术家Andy Warhol的话 )，任何人都可以把创作称为对“艺术”的贡献。
sentences: The phrase ‘the arts’ includes painting, sculpture, music, literature, dance and theatre performance, and whatever else (to quote the famous US artist Andy Warhol) anyone can get away with in calling their creation a contribution to ‘the arts’.
“艺术”一词包括绘画、雕塑、音乐、文学、舞蹈和戏剧表演等(引用美国著名艺术家Andy Warhol的话 )，任何人都可以把创作称为对“艺术”的贡献。
But the generalisation that the arts, whatever else they are, are always an end in themselves, applies to them all.
但是，艺术，不管它们是什么，本身总是一个目的，都适用于它们。
The arts are one major form of response to the world.
艺术是对世界的一种主要反应形式。

They are often an attempt to capture an aspect of the world, to draw attention to something about it, to comment on it, to present a surprising or fresh angle on it, to represent it for the sake of exploring something about it, or enjoying or celebrating it.
它们往往试图捕捉世界的一个方面，提请人们注意它的某些方面，对此发表评论，提出一个令人吃惊或全新的角度，为了探索它的某些方面或享受或庆祝它而代表它。
They can help people to focus on, for example, the colour or shape of an object, its eccentricity or typicality, and the interest or perhaps disgust it provokes in them.
例如，它们可以帮助人们关注物体的颜色或形状，其偏心或典型性，以及它引起人们的兴趣或厌恶。

paragraphs.brief: 比较一下，想笑一个笑话
sentences: For a loose comparison, think of laughing at a joke.
比较一下，想笑一个笑话

We do not laugh so that we can achieve a further goal—in order to be healthy or relaxed, say, even if we thereby succeed in being healthier or more relaxed—but simply because the joke has elicited that reaction.
我们不笑，以便我们能够实现进一步的目标——例如，即使我们因此成功地变得更健康或更放松——但仅仅是因为笑话引起了这种反应。
But although it is merely a reaction, laughing is, in fact, good for something nevertheless; it does make people feel better.
但是，尽管这只是一种反应，但笑实际上还是有好处的；它确实使人们感觉更好。
The arts are a reaction in the same way.
艺术也是同样的反应
French artist Cézanne painted Mont Sainte-Victoire repeatedly because he was fascinated by it, not because he thought that painting it would say something about politics or society or human hopes.
法国艺术家塞赞恩多次画圣维斯托瓦山，因为他对它很着迷，并不是因为他觉得画它会表达政治、社会或人类的希望。

Being fascinated by something, attracted to it, repelled by it, keen to reveal an unusual aspect of it, are all responses to that thing; the making of the arts is one outstanding way of expressing such responses.
被某种东西吸引，被它所吸引，被其驱使，渴望揭示其中的一个不寻常的方面，这些都是对这件事的反应；艺术的创造是表达这种反应的一种杰出方式。

paragraphs.brief: 但艺术不仅是对世界事物的一种反应也是对世界经验的一种反应，而世界经验就存在于艺术家本人身上。
sentences: But the arts are a response not only to things in the world but also to experience of the world, which lies inside the artist himself.
但艺术不仅是对世界事物的一种反应也是对世界经验的一种反应，而世界经验就存在于艺术家本人身上。
And they are also often an expression of what presses from within the artist without being elicited by externals.
也经常是艺术家内部压力的表达而不是外界的诱惑。
Music is a prime example.
音乐是一个很好的例子。
A symphony, unless it is devised to represent bird song, rain, the sea and the like, is an abstract expression of a composer’s conception.
一种交响乐，除非是用来代表鸟歌、雨、海等的，是作曲家概念的抽象表达。
We may be able to describe what the Russian composer Tchaikovsky is doing in his ballet music, but how can we describe what he is expressing in his piano concertos?
我们也许可以描述一下俄国作曲家柴可夫斯基在他的芭蕾舞曲中在做什么，但我们如何描述他在他的钢琴协奏曲中表达什么？
Composers may experiment with melody and rhythm in very abstract, sometimes mathematical, ways.
作曲家可以以非常抽象，有时是数学的方式来实验旋律和节奏。

paragraphs.brief: 当艺术家开始工作回应和表达想法，无论他们是否也想提出一个观点，娱乐，分散注意力，支持革命和其他，他们正在产生的东西别人会以某种方式作出反应。
sentences: When artists get to work responding to and expressing ideas, whether or not they also want to make a point, entertain, distract, support a revolution and the rest, they are producing something that someone else will react to in some way.
当艺术家开始工作回应和表达想法，无论他们是否也想提出一个观点，娱乐，分散注意力，支持革命和其他，他们正在产生的东西别人会以某种方式作出反应。
They seek to connect with their audience and express an idea or emotion which has the capacity to enrich our experience of life itself.
他们试图与观众沟通，表达一种想法或情感，这种想法或情感能够丰富我们的生活经验。

items.en: a claim that artists may have no clear objective when creating a piece of art
items.zh: 声称艺术家在创作艺术品时可能没有明确的目标
items.why: 有时艺术家只是觉得非创作不可，并未先确定作品要实现的明确目的。

items.en: a description of how artists hope to benefit other people
items.zh: 描述艺术家希望如何造福于他人
items.why: 描述艺术家希望给他人带来好处 (与受众连接、丰富生命体验)。

items.en: a comparison between the arts and things made to perform a particular function
items.zh: 艺术和为履行特定职能而制造的东西之间的比较
items.why: 把艺术与“为特定功能而做的东西对比: 艺术本质上是目的本身。

items.en: a claim that it’s possible to convince the world that anything you have made is a work of art
items.zh: 说自己能让世界相信你所做的一切都是艺术品
items.why: D段引述沃霍尔，说明只要能说服别人，自制的东西也可能被视为艺术作品。

items.en: an example of something that has an unintentional benefit for us
items.zh: 一个对我们有无意好处的例子
items.why: 听到笑话而笑本只是反应，却会让人感觉更好，作者以这种非出于原意的好处作类比。

items.en: But there are many clear examples of their usefulness, such as the interdependent relationship between music and ________, or between the visual arts and the ____ (Q20) business.
items.zh: 艺术的实用性有许多明显的例子，例如音乐与________相互依存，视觉艺术与________（Q20）行业也相互依存。
items.why: 强调音乐与舞蹈的相互依存。

items.en: But there are many clear examples of their usefulness, such as the interdependent relationship between music and ____ (Q19), or between the visual arts and the ________ business.
items.zh: 艺术的实用性有许多明显的例子，例如音乐与________（Q19）相互依存，视觉艺术与________行业也相互依存。
items.why: 视觉艺术与广告行业的联系。

items.en: A dramatist may use a ________ to draw our attention to various issues in society, for example some kind of injustice which needs correcting.
items.zh: 剧作家可以借一部________引导我们关注社会问题，例如某种有待纠正的不公现象。
items.why: 剧作家用戏剧引起社会关注。

items.en: Apart from these obvious practical benefits, there are other benefits that we gain from things, such as the ________ we find in an artist’s work.
items.zh: 除了这些显而易见的实际用途，我们还能从事物中得到其他收获，例如在艺术家的作品中发现________。
items.why: 除实用外，还从艺术中获得美。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: In paragraph D, which TWO of the following effects does the writer say the arts can have?
items.zh: 在D段，作者说艺术可以产生以下两种效果？
correct: They can make us see things from a different perspective.
他们可以让我们从不同的角度看待事物。
They can encourage us to think about our reactions to things around us.
他们可以鼓励我们思考我们对周围事物的反应。

items.en: Which TWO of the following statements about composers and music does the writer make?
items.zh: 作者对作曲家和音乐的以下两个说法是什么呢？
correct: Music tends to spring from the composer’s individual experiences.
音乐往往来自作曲家的个人经历。
Music can be quite unrelated to the natural world.
音乐可能和自然界无关

points: 听到笑话而笑本只是反应，却会让人感觉更好，作者以这种非出于原意的好处作类比。
剧作家用戏剧引起社会关注。
clauses: …, no aim or goal is necessarily required to explain or, still less, to justify its existence.
连接词 because 引出“Because the work is its own justification”，说明主句的原因关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 because 把这一层关系补进去。
But to say …, even though they may sometimes do so, is not to say that they are good for nothing.
“that the arts do not have to serve an aim beyond themselves”补足 say 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 say 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Sometimes people question why we need ‘the arts’; what functions do art, music, dance and literature serve?
有时人们会质疑为什么我们需要“艺术”;艺术、音乐、舞蹈和文学有什么功能？
